question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Acceleration of a Particle
question.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(-2i-8j)\,\text{m/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-2i-8j,\,v=2i,\,t=4,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 2i & =(-2i-8j)+a(4) \\ 4i+8j & =4a \\ a & =\frac{1}{4}(4i+8j) \\  & =(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
